intent: Trace the estimated daily oxygen need over the period from March 2020 through March 2021 and identify when the largest increase occurred.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
Trace the estimated daily oxygen need over March 2020 through March 2021 and identify when the largest increase occurred.

The largest month-over-month increase in estimated daily oxygen need occurs between February 2021 and March 2021, rising from 1.500578 to 10.501155 million m³ (an increase of about 9.000577 million m³).

units.claim: All 1 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: The estimated daily oxygen need rises from 0.200751 million m³ in March 2020 to a peak of 10.501155 million m³ in March 2021, with an intermediate peak of 4.501733 million m³ in September 2020 followed by a decline to 1.500578 million m³ in February 2021 before the final surge.
units.computation: Compare values across the ordered sequence: Mar 2020 = 0.200751, Sep 2020 = 4.501733, Feb 2021 = 1.500578, Mar 2021 = 10.501155.
accept: Describes an overall upward trend from March 2020 to March 2021.
Mentions the intermediate peak around September 2020 and subsequent decline before the final rise.
reject: Claims a monotonic increase with no intermediate decline.
Omits the final value in March 2021.

units.claim: The largest month-over-month increase in estimated daily oxygen need occurs between February 2021 and March 2021, rising from 1.500578 to 10.501155 million m³ (an increase of about 9.000577 million m³).
units.computation: Compute consecutive differences; the largest is Mar 2021 minus Feb 2021 = 10.501155 - 1.500578 = 9.000577 million m³.
accept: Identifies February 2021 to March 2021 as the interval with the largest increase.
States the increase amount or the endpoint values for that interval.
reject: Identifies a different interval as the largest increase.
Fails to specify the interval of the largest increase.

optional_valid: Mentions the absolute difference between March 2020 and March 2021 (about 10.300404 million m³).
Notes that the minimum value is 0.200751 million m³ in March 2020.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for the oxygen need changes.
Claims about data beyond March 2021 or before March 2020.
Comparisons across multiple panels (only one panel exists).
review_notes: The intent asks for two analytical operations: tracing the trend over the period and identifying the largest increase. These map to U1 and U2.
The x-axis label mentions April 2021 but the data ends at March 2021; units use only the supplied table rows.
